title: Check if There is a Valid Partition For The Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine if it can be partitioned into one or more contiguous subarrays such that each subarray meets one of the following conditions: - The subarray consists of exactly two equal elements.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine if it can be partitioned into one or more contiguous subarrays such that each subarray meets one of the following conditions: - The subarray consists of exactly two equal elements. - The subarray consists of exactly three equal elements. - The subarray consists of three consecutive elements that are increasing by exactly 1. Return true if such a partition exists, otherwise return false.
constraints: Partition the entire array into contiguous groups with no unused elements.
A valid group is either two equal values, three equal values, or three consecutive increasing values.
For an increasing triple [a,b,c], require b=a+1 and c=b+1.
hints: Let possible[i] mean that the first i values have a valid complete partition.
An equal or consecutive triple extends possible[i-3].
Every legal final group has length two or three, so these transitions examine every possible last group and no invalid split.
editorial: Every legal final group has length two or three, so these transitions examine every possible last group and no invalid split.

tests.explanation: Split the array as [4,4] and [4,5,6]; both groups satisfy an allowed rule.
Neither taking [1,1] nor [1,1,1] leaves a valid group for the remaining suffix, so no full partition exists.
